summary: The first contribution establishes a reasoned one-step accuracy identity and its scope. It provides no empirical evidence that self-correction outperforms cost-matched resampling. No prior findings or graph relations were supplied, and no trusted execution occurred.
open_questions: Under matched inference budgets, does revision outperform independent resampling with a frozen selection rule?
How do correction and regression rates differ between intrinsic critique and explicitly specified external feedback?
next_question: On at least 200 held-out tasks with deterministic scoring, can a prespecified paired comparison estimate revision versus cost-matched resampling, including transition counts, feedback access and uncertainty?

relations.reason: The identity establishes improvement relative to initial accuracy, without establishing superiority over another budget-matched method.
The stated population and outcome assumptions determine when the two-state identity applies directly.

findings.text: For initial accuracy p, conditional correction rate c and conditional regression rate r, final accuracy is p(1-r)+(1-p)c. Accuracy increases exactly when (1-p)c>pr. The stated examples yield 0.66 and 0.52. Independence between initial and final correctness is unnecessary.
findings.quote: Thus the gain is (one minus p) multiplied by c, minus p multiplied by r.
findings.verification:
Derived by partitioning the joint correctness table into initially correct and initially wrong cases; both numerical examples were checked by arithmetic. Zero-mass states contribute zero without requiring defined conditional rates. No harness, code or model evaluation was executed.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

findings.text: Improvement over initial accuracy does not establish an advantage over cost-matched resampling. That comparison remains untested.
findings.quote: This condition by itself says nothing about whether revision beats cost-matched independent resampling.
findings.verification:
The transition identity contains no resampling accuracy or inference-cost terms, so it cannot establish comparative efficiency. No cost-matched comparison was executed.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

findings.text: The identity assumes a common task population, binary correctness and a returned revision for every task. Selective revision, abstention or other scoring requires explicit outcome and denominator handling; estimating transition rates requires paired observations and uncertainty estimates.
findings.quote: The comparison is over the same task population with a binary correctness criterion and a revision returned for every task.
findings.verification:
Reviewed the assumptions needed for the two-state partition. Selective revision can retain the identity if unchanged answers count as final outputs for every task; conditioning only on selected tasks changes the estimand. No task observations or extended outcome model were evaluated.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.
